prerequisites: Basic concepts of linear system theory and linear differential equations
Basic knowledge of transformations such as Laplace and Z-transformations

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the general architecture of digital signal processing systems and can discuss their main advantages and disadvantages compared to analog signal processing.

The student can describe continuous and discrete time signals and images in the frequency domain using the continuous and discrete Fourier transform, and can analyze the effects of sampling and interpolation on this frequency description within this theoretical framework.
The student can analyze the behavior of linear filters in the frequency domain, and can design simple digital filters and their realization structure, also in multirate systems.
The student can situate common applications from the audiovisual domain within the theoretical framework for signal processing.

syllabus_topics: Signal and system analysis with eigenfunctions
Basic theory of analytical signal transformations
Analysis and realization of digital filters
Transformation of decimated and interpolated sequences

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the exam period

assessment_rules: The exam consists of both theory questions and exercises. A formula sheet is provided and may be used during the exam.
